summary: SteerVAD proposes a tuning-free video anomaly detection framework that (1) selects a small set of attention heads (LAEs) in a frozen MLLM via a between/within-class scatter ratio, and (2) trains a lightweight gated adapter (HMC = GSG scalar + per-head low-rank tanh vectors) that multiplicatively modulates those head outputs, followed by a logistic regression scorer. The framing around manifold geometry is intuitive and the data efficiency (1% calibration, ~16 videos) plus 10-seed stability of LAE selection are appealing, but the empirical gains over the strongest tuning-free baseline are small (~+0.4 AUC on UCF, +0.9 AP on XD), the method is evaluated on a single backbone, and the 'tuning-free' terminology is inconsistent with the fact that HMC + scorer are supervised on labeled anomalies. The contribution is real but modest and oversold; it needs additional experiments (multiple backbones, error bars on the main table, honest re-framing of supervision) before it is a clear ICLR accept.
strengths: Clear, well-motivated framing: identifying which attention heads carry the anomaly signal and then rectifying only those, rather than the whole model, is a sensible way to specialize a frozen MLLM.
The RSA scatter-ratio criterion is simple, gradient-free, and cheap; the ablation in Table 2 Part B convincingly shows it beats layer-position heuristics and random selection.

Table 3's 10-seed calibration stability is a strong piece of evidence: the same four heads (L18H4, L23H24, L21H21, L22H7) are recovered every time with σ ≈ 0.04% AUC, arguing that the discovered 'circuits' are intrinsic to the backbone rather than seed/data artifacts.
The data-efficiency analysis in Table 4 (1% ≈ 100% within +0.27 AUC) is a genuinely useful positive result for a low-supervision regime.

The HMC design is decoupled into an interpretable global gate (should we intervene?) and per-head local anisotropic scaling (how?), and the ablation cleanly shows both matter and that anisotropic multiplicative steering beats static or additive variants.
The sparsity regularizer on s_global for normal samples is a nice, well-motivated inductive bias for reducing false positives.

key_concerns.issue: The 'tuning-free' framing is misleading. The HMC (GSG + K low-rank LGM adapters) and the logistic regression scorer are trained with labeled anomaly/normal frames via BCE for 1000 epochs. The MLLM weights are frozen, but this is standard few-shot supervised adapter training on top of frozen features, not zero-/tuning-free inference. Table 1 groups the method with 'Tuning-Free Multimodal VAD' methods, several of which (LAVAD, EventVAD) are genuinely zero-shot; the comparison is not apples-to-apples.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Rename the setting (e.g., 'frozen-backbone few-shot' or 'label-efficient probe/steer') and split Table 1 into (a) purely zero-shot MLLM methods and (b) methods that use labeled anomalies to train a small module on frozen features (VERA, HiProbeVAD, SteerVAD). Make the supervision assumption explicit in the abstract and Section 1.

key_concerns.issue: Empirical gains over the closest tuning-free baseline are small and reported without variance. On UCF-Crime, HiProbeVAD is 86.72 vs SteerVAD 87.15 (+0.43 AUC); on XD-Violence, 82.15 vs 83.02 (+0.87 AP). Table 3 shows σ ≈ 0.04% AUC across seeds for the identical LAEs, but this measures LAE-selection stability given the fixed method — not the seed-to-seed variance of the final AUC across baselines. Without matched-seed evaluation and confidence intervals on Table 1, the SOTA claim is not statistically established.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over ≥5 seeds for the main comparison table (or at minimum for SteerVAD and the two strongest tuning-free baselines re-run under matched conditions), and a significance test versus HiProbeVAD/VERA. Temper 'new state-of-the-art' to reflect the effect size.

key_concerns.issue: Generality is claimed but under-evidenced. All experiments use one MLLM backbone (InternVL3). The paper's central premise — that a small set of intrinsic 'latent anomaly experts' exists and can be steered — cannot be validated from a single model. It's also unclear whether the four selected heads are dataset-agnostic (do UCF-Crime-selected heads transfer to XD-Violence and vice versa?).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one additional MLLM backbone (e.g., LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2-VL, or InternVL2), and a cross-dataset LAE-transfer experiment (train LAE + HMC on UCF, evaluate on XD without recalibration, and vice versa). Report how many heads are shared.

key_concerns.issue: The 'manifold rectification / anisotropic scaling' framing is heavier than the underlying math. Eq. 4 is h'_i = h_i ⊙ (1 + s_global · g_i) — a scalar-gated element-wise multiplicative adapter with tanh-bounded per-dim gates. This is a well-known family (LoRA-style bottleneck adapters + gated feature modulation), not a novel geometric operation. Calling this 'active geometric intervention on representation manifolds' inflates the contribution.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Dial back the geometric/manifold language in the abstract and intro, position honestly as 'a gated multiplicative adapter applied to a small set of task-aligned attention heads,' and move the manifold discussion to a motivational rather than mechanistic role. Keep RSA and the head-selection story as the main novelty.

key_concerns.issue: Several hyperparameter and design choices are unablated: λ_reg = 0.1, Gaussian σ_g = 6, low-rank r, and the choice to use the 'first generated token's final hidden state' as the global context c. The last is a strong assumption — that a single autoregressive token summarizes a scene — and it is neither validated nor compared to alternatives (mean-pool over visual tokens, [CLS]-like token, etc.).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add ablations for λ_reg, σ_g, r, and (most importantly) different choices of the global context vector c. A brief sensitivity table would suffice.

key_concerns.issue: The post-hoc explainability step (re-submitting flagged segments to the MLLM for a textual explanation) is described but never evaluated qualitatively or quantitatively, yet contributes to the paper's narrative of trustworthy VAD.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either add a small qualitative case study / human-rated explanation quality analysis, or remove the claim from the contributions.

key_concerns.issue: Related-work positioning versus model-editing / activation-steering literature (e.g., activation additions, task vectors, function vectors, feature-steering in LLMs) is thin. The paper says this line is unexplored for spatio-temporal reasoning, but does not concretely compare its mechanism to activation-addition or LoRA-on-selected-heads variants.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a subsection explicitly relating h_i ⊙ (1 + s·g_i) to activation additions (h + Δh), scaling steering vectors, and adapters on selected heads; ideally include an ablation replacing anisotropic multiplicative scaling with an additive activation-steering baseline of matched capacity.

key_concerns.issue: Clarity issues: the extracted text has multiple typos ('effectively disentangling', 'inherently aligned'), inconsistent notation (μ appears to be missing in Eq. 1 in the extraction), and the framework figure is described in text but the caption alone leaves several details ambiguous (e.g., whether the anomaly scorer is per-segment or per-frame, exact temporal aggregation).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Copy-edit the manuscript, restate Eq. 1 with explicit μ (centroid) notation, and add a short paragraph in Section 3.5 defining segment/frame granularity for scoring.

questions_for_authors: How does SteerVAD compare to HiProbeVAD and VERA under matched seeds and matched backbones? Please report paired-seed AUC/AP with confidence intervals or a significance test.
Do the four selected LAEs (L18H4, L23H24, L21H21, L22H7) transfer between UCF-Crime and XD-Violence? If you calibrate on UCF and evaluate on XD (and vice versa), how much does performance change?
Does the method work with other frozen MLLM backbones (LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2-VL, InternVL2)? Are similar 'anomaly-expert' heads recovered, and is the choice of layer/index consistent?

The global context c is the first generated token's final hidden state. What does this token attend to before generation, and how sensitive is performance to this choice versus visual-token pooling or a later token?
Is the anomaly scorer trained per-frame or per-segment? What is the label at training time — segment-level from video-level MIL, or frame-level? Please clarify what labels the 1% subset provides.

Table 2 Part A compares HMC variants but does not include a matched-parameter LoRA-on-attention-output baseline. How does SteerVAD compare to standard LoRA/adapter fine-tuning restricted to the same K heads?

How is the anisotropic scaling formula (1 + s·g) chosen versus, e.g., additive activation steering h + s·g or gated mixture h + s·(W g)? The Part A ablation shows additive < multiplicative, but with different parameterizations — please clarify the controls.
How sensitive is performance to λ_reg, σ_g, and the low-rank r? Are the reported numbers with a single tuned setting, or averaged over the search?
Given the 'tuning-free' claim: what exactly is trained? Please state the parameter count of HMC + scorer and clarify how it differs from a small LoRA adapter.
calibration_check: Claims are partially miscalibrated: 'tuning-free' is inaccurate since HMC + scorer are supervised, the 'manifold rectification / geometric intervention' language overstates what is mathematically a gated multiplicative adapter on selected heads, and 'state-of-the-art' rests on ~0.4–0.9 point improvements reported without error bars in the main comparison.

significance.justification: Head-selection + light-weight steering on frozen MLLMs is a useful direction, but the absolute gains over the closest tuning-free baseline are small and confined to two VAD benchmarks.

novelty.justification: RSA + a gated per-head multiplicative adapter is a sensible packaging of known ideas (activation steering, LoRA-style bottleneck adapters, attention-head localization); the manifold framing is more re-branding than a new mechanism.

rigor.justification: The method is described clearly and the ablations of HMC components and head-selection strategy are appropriate, but the analysis of why the multiplicative form beats alternatives and controls for parameter count are missing.

statistical_soundness.justification: The 10-seed LAE-selection stability (σ ≈ 0.04% AUC) is nicely done, but the main Table 1 has no error bars and no significance test versus HiProbeVAD/VERA, so the SOTA claim rests on differences within plausible seed noise.

calibration_honesty.justification: 'Tuning-free' framing conflicts with 1000-epoch supervised training of HMC + logistic scorer on labeled anomalies; 'active geometric intervention on representation manifolds' oversells a gated element-wise adapter; SOTA claim is not properly qualified.

clarity.justification: The narrative arc from manifold hypothesis to RSA to HMC is easy to follow and equations are compact, but there are typos, some notation gaps (missing μ symbol in Eq. 1 as extracted), and unclear scoring granularity (segment vs frame).

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR-style structure with clear Intro, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Conclusion; appendices referenced appropriately for topological details and extra visualizations.

reproducibility.justification: Backbone, segment length, F, K, optimizer, LR, epochs, batch size, λ_reg, σ_g, and hardware are all specified; missing are the low-rank r, scorer/HMC parameter counts, and exact label granularity of the 1% subset.

related_work.justification: Tuning-free VAD and traditional VAD are well surveyed, but activation-steering / model-editing / adapter literature is only lightly touched, and no direct methodological baseline from that line is included.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative artifacts (UMAP manifolds, framework diagram, before/after t-SNE), but Figure 1's caption is generic and Figure 4 relies on a well-known 'clusters became more separated' narrative that is only weakly diagnostic.

breadth_generality.justification: Only one MLLM backbone (InternVL3) and two datasets (UCF-Crime, XD-Violence); no cross-backbone or cross-dataset LAE-transfer analysis to support the generality of the 'latent anomaly experts' claim.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: methodologically reasonable and empirically positive, but small effect sizes without variance, single-backbone evaluation, and inflated framing (both 'tuning-free' and 'manifold rectification') keep it below the ICLR accept bar as submitted.
